_doc: Strum patterns for one 4/4 bar as 4 space-separated BEAT CELLS (beats 1 2 3 4). Each cell's LENGTH is its subdivision: 1=quarter, 2=eighths, 3=triplet, 4=sixteenths. Char per slot: D=downstroke, U=upstroke, x=muted chuck, .=no strike (slot 0 of a cell is the downbeat). Encoded in Hookpad as re-struck chords with empty notes. See music_chord_riff_fingerprint (Layer 2 = strike rhythm).
_doc2: A PUSH is the &4 of one bar sustaining across the next downbeat, so bar 2 has no strike on beat 1. In Simple Kind of Life the push is ALSO the chord change: the verse is Dm(add9) x5 then plain Dm on the pushed &4, then plain Dm for bar 2 -- and the same again on C. Four chords, not two. The add resolving away exactly at the push is what moves the pair; reading it as one chord re-struck loses the whole point. Check the 'adds' field before concluding two chords are the same chord.
